forcedChoices.reason: Gabriel speaks to one person (Elizabeth); the same for Mary in 122:3.1 and the messenger to Joseph in 122:4.1.
«del reino» can be read as the kingdom of heaven; here realm means the world where the child is born.
The English capitalizes «Him»; the capital is kept.
«doncella» reads as archaic; «joven» keeps the contrast with «virgen» that the sentence depends on.
Spanish has no common gentile noun for «Judean» that is not also «judío»; the place name keeps the sense.
The hymn is sung to the assembled people; the plural imperative fits and avoids «vosotros».
The English is ambiguous (unveiling to or of the gentiles); a literal form keeps both readings open.
A bare «bolsa» loses the sense of money that «purse» carries.
